service.description: Load offline-generated normative graph JSONL files (from tools/norm-indexer) into moqui.math.Graph/GraphVertex/GraphEdge, with vertex/edge metadata materialized as moqui.math.Parameter rows keyed by the CyberNorm* ParameterDef records. Mirrors the load#ArtifactGraph pattern in moqui-mcp, adapted to the separate vertex-metadata.jsonl/edge-metadata.jsonl files produced by generate_norm_graph.py.

Search normative clauses materialized in the CyberNormVertexMeta pivot view. OpenSearch/DataDocument-backed retrieval is a later milestone (Phase 6); this first version queries the Moqui-persisted graph directly so the graph is usable as soon as it is loaded, same "search#Artifacts as legacy direct path" precedent used in moqui-mcp.

actions.script: def find = ec.entity.find('moqui.cyber.graph.CyberNormVertexMeta') .condition('vertexType', 'NormClause') .condition('clauseText', 'like', "%${queryText}%") .orderBy('clauseNumber') if (documentId) find = find.condition('documentId', documentId) List candidates = find.list() int effectiveLimit = (limit ?: 8) as int results = candidates.take(effectiveLimit).collect { row -> [ graphVertexId : row.graphVertexId, logicalId : row.logicalId, documentId : row.documentId, clauseNumber : row.clauseNumber, clauseTitle : row.clauseTitle, sourceFile : row.sourceFile, provenanceClass: row.provenanceClass, snippet : row.clauseText ? (row.clauseText.length() > 300 ? row.clauseText.substring(0, 300) + '...' : row.clauseText) : '' ] }

service.description: Systematic, paginated listing of every NormClause vertex of one document, ordered by clauseNumber, with full untruncated clauseText - unlike search#NormClauses (a text-match search returning a 300-char snippet), this is for methodically walking an entire document clause-by-clause during vocabulary extraction (norm-product-classification skill, Workflow A), where the full clause text is needed to judge whether it defines a component type/category or a testable requirement.

actions.script: def find = ec.entity.find('moqui.cyber.graph.CyberNormVertexMeta') .condition('vertexType', 'NormClause') .condition('documentId', documentId) .orderBy('clauseNumber') List allClauses = find.list() totalCount = allClauses.size() int effectiveOffset = (offset ?: 0) as int int effectiveLimit = (limit ?: 50) as int clauses = allClauses.drop(effectiveOffset).take(effectiveLimit).collect { row -> [ graphVertexId : row.graphVertexId, logicalId : row.logicalId, documentId : row.documentId, clauseNumber : row.clauseNumber, clauseTitle : row.clauseTitle, clauseText : row.clauseText, sourceFile : row.sourceFile, provenanceClass: row.provenanceClass ] }

service.description:
Read-only: given one clause's graphVertexId, returns every REFERENCES/ HARMONIZES_WITH edge touching it (in either direction), each resolved to the real documentId/clauseNumber/clauseTitle of the other endpoint - not just the raw edge. Wraps moqui.cyber.graph.CyberNormEdgeMeta (CyberNormGraphExtensions.xml), built in Phase 1 but never queried by any service until now (776 REFERENCES + 8 HARMONIZES_WITH edges already sit in OtCyberNormGraph, unused).
This is the concrete signal for deciding ProductFeatureGroup granularity during vocabulary extraction (norm-product-classification skill, Workflow A): a clause that references, or is referenced by, several others (even across different documents) is real evidence those clauses belong in one ProductFeatureGroup together - not an arbitrary editorial choice. Confirmed on real data: IEC 62443-3-3's Annex B and EN 40000-1-3's Annex ZA are both real correspondence/mapping tables the norms themselves wrote, and both show up as the highest-out-degree REFERENCES clauses in the whole graph.

Index norm clauses materialized in CyberNormVertexMeta into OpenSearch, with embeddings, reusing moqui-mcp's existing ElasticBackendAdapter and get#QueryEmbedding service exactly as-is (same embedding provider/model/dimensions, same L1/L2 cache) instead of duplicating that logic.

Hybrid BM25 + kNN semantic search over the OpenSearch norm-clause index built by index#NormDocuments. Falls back gracefully with a clear error if the index/embedding is not available yet -- callers should use search#NormClauses (direct entity query) until the OpenSearch index has actually been populated.

actions.script:
import org.moqui.agent.search.ElasticBackendAdapter
String effectiveIndex = (indexName ?: 'moqui_cyber_norms_v1').toString() def adapter = new ElasticBackendAdapter(ec) if (!adapter.indexExists(effectiveIndex)) { throw new IllegalStateException("Index ${effectiveIndex} does not exist yet; run index#NormDocuments first.") } Map embeddingResult = ec.service.sync().name('org.moqui.agent.AgentDocumentServices.get#QueryEmbedding') .parameters([queryText: queryText]).call() List queryVector = embeddingResult.embedding as List
List<Map> shouldClauses = [ [match: [clauseText: [query: queryText]]], [knn: [embedding: [vector: queryVector, k: (limit ?: 8)]]] ] Map boolQuery = [bool: [should: shouldClauses]] if (documentId) boolQuery.bool.filter = [[term: [documentId: documentId]]]
Map querySpec = [ size : (limit ?: 8), query: boolQuery, _source: ['graphVertexId', 'logicalId', 'documentId', 'clauseNumber', 'clauseTitle', 'clauseText', 'sourceFile', 'provenanceClass'] ] Map searchResult = adapter.search(effectiveIndex, querySpec) List hits = ((searchResult.hits ?: [:]).hits ?: []) as List results = hits.collect { hit -> Map source = (hit.source ?: hit._source ?: [:]) as Map [ graphVertexId : source.graphVertexId, logicalId : source.logicalId, documentId : source.documentId, clauseNumber : source.clauseNumber, clauseTitle : source.clauseTitle, sourceFile : source.sourceFile, provenanceClass: source.provenanceClass, score : hit.score ?: hit._score, snippet : source.clauseText ? ((source.clauseText as String).length() > 300 ? (source.clauseText as String).substring(0, 300) + '...' : source.clauseText) : '' ] }
